From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@jpm-audit.com>

Subject: SOC 2 Type II — question on partial-month migration window

Hi Olga,

We're reviewing the evidence for FinCo's connection to Redwood and have a quick question about the audit period coverage. Our current testing window is 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30 (SOC 2 Type II). Per our logs, FinCo executed a migration on 2026-06-30 that completed at approximately 16:45 PDT and some related traffic continued into 2026-07-01 UTC.

Two quick clarifications we need from Redwood:
1) For the purposes of the Type II report, do you treat the last day of the audit period (2026-06-30) as inclusive up to 23:59:59 UTC, or do you define inclusion differently (e.g., local datestamp cutoff)?
2) If activity spans across the midnight boundary (local timezone to UTC overlap), can you provide a point-in-time export (snapshot) or roll-forward statement that documents system state at the end of 2026-06-30? If not, would a bridge letter describing the migration window plus sampled logs be acceptable to the auditor?

We want to be explicit so our testing and sampling strategy is aligned. Appreciate a short confirmation and any attachments you can share (snapshot or roll-forward evidence).

Thanks,
Michael Lee
Senior IT Auditor
JPM Audit LLC

- We can provide a point-in-time export of relevant system state and sampled logs capturing the 2026-06-30 end-of-day snapshot. We can also issue a short bridge letter explaining the migration window and exactly which components had state transitions during the window.

1) logs snapshot (token-level ingress/egress log sample) captured at 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z — CSV/JSON export

3) one-page bridge letter describing the migration, exact timestamps, and controls that remained in effect during and after the migration

I'll loop in the infra/security folks to assemble the exports. Expect a follow-up with attachments and a draft bridge letter within 48 hours. Please tell us if you need the snapshot in a particular timezone or format.
